label: DOCUMENTED
headline: Mary: 1 in 14 girls
text: Named for the Virgin Mary, Christianity's most honored woman, Mary went to 7.2% of US girls in 1880, more than double #2 Anna.
image_credit: Sassoferrato, The Virgin in Prayer (1640s), public domain

label: THEORY
headline: Old-world classics rule
text: Bible, saints and royalty: Anna (St. Anne), Elizabeth, Margaret (a top name in Ireland), Emma (Jane Austen's heroine). Many came with immigrants.
image_credit: Castle Garden immigrant depot, NY, Charles Magnus print, CC0

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: Nicknames on the birth certificate
text: Victorians loved cozy -ie names. Minnie (from Wilhelmina or Mary) and Bessie (from Elizabeth) were given as full names, not just pet names.

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: The Lady with the Lamp
text: Crimean War nurse Florence Nightingale, named for her Italian birthplace, turned Florence into a heroine's name. It kept climbing for decades.
image_credit: Florence Nightingale, c.1857, Henry Hering, public domain

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: America's first celebrity baby
text: Grover Cleveland's daughter "Baby Ruth" was born in Oct 1891 to a press frenzy. Ruth leapt from #46 in 1890 to #5 in 1892.
image_credit: Ruth Cleveland (1897), unknown photographer, public domain

label: THEORY
headline: Helen's quiet climb to #3
text: Helen rose from #35 to #3 with no single trigger. Likely appeal: a classic Greek name (Helen of Troy) that suited the era's taste for old classics.
image_credit: Evelyn De Morgan, Helen of Troy (1898), public domain

label: THEORY
headline: Dorothy and the Wizard of Oz?
text: Dorothy hit the top 10 by 1904, after The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900) became a bestseller. It was already rising, so the book likely just helped.
image_credit: W. W. Denslow, Wizard of Oz illustration (1900), public domain

label: THEORY
headline: Betty: the flapper-era nickname
text: Once just a nickname for Elizabeth, Betty went solo as film stars like Betty Compson used it as a stage name. Short and peppy, it fit the '20s.
image_credit: Betty Compson, 1921, Alfred Cheney Johnston, public domain

label: THEORY
headline: Barbara Stanwyck & Princess Pat
text: Barbara hit the top 10 in 1927, the year Barbara Stanwyck became a star. Patricia climbed after WWI made Britain's "Princess Pat" famous.
image_credit: Barbara Stanwyck (c.1930), studio still, public domain

label: THEORY
headline: Joan Crawford's Joan
text: Joan was #95 in 1924. In 1925 MGM renamed Lucille LeSueur "Joan Crawford"; as she became a star, Joan shot to #5 by 1931. The timing fits.
image_credit: Joan Crawford, 1928, Ruth Harriet Louise, public domain

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: Shirley Temple mania
text: Child star Shirley Temple broke out in 1934's Stand Up and Cheer! and Bright Eyes. Shirley nearly doubled in 1935, hitting #2.
image_credit: Shirley Temple, Bright Eyes (1934), Fox, public domain

label: THEORY
headline: Hollywood's Linda and Judy
text: Linda jumped 65% in 1940 as Linda Darnell became a Fox star. Judith rose alongside Judy Garland's fame (The Wizard of Oz, 1939).
image_credit: Linda Darnell, 20th Century Fox publicity, public domain

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: Linda ends Mary's 67-year run
text: Buddy Clark's 1947 hit "Linda" was written for a lawyer's toddler, Linda Eastman, later Linda McCartney. Linda dethroned Mary for the first time.
image_credit: Buddy Clark, c.1947, William P. Gottlieb/LoC, public domain

label: THEORY
headline: Deborah Kerr's Hollywood rise
text: Already rising, Deborah boomed as Deborah Kerr (and Debra Paget) became stars. It was #4 by 1951 and spun off the Debra spelling too.
image_credit: Deborah Kerr, Black Narcissus (1947) trailer, public domain

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: Mary takes back #1
text: Mary didn't surge; it was slowly slipping. Linda just crashed faster, from 4.6% of girls in 1950 to 3.2% in 1953, so Mary was back on top.
image_credit: Sassoferrato, The Virgin in Prayer (1640s), public domain

label: THEORY
headline: Lisa's long climb to #1
text: Nat King Cole's Oscar-winning "Mona Lisa" (1950) sparked a wave of baby Monas. Lisa went from #220 in 1950 to #1 by 1962; the song may have helped.
image_credit: Nat King Cole, 1947, William P. Gottlieb/LoC, public domain

label: THEORY
headline: Kim Novak makes Kim feminine
text: Kim was a boy's name until 1954, when stars Kim Hunter and Kim Novak (Picnic, Vertigo) made it a girl's name. Kimberly rode along to #2 by 1966.
image_credit: Kim Novak, Columbia Pictures still (1959), public domain

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: Tammy's movie franchise
text: Debbie Reynolds' 1957 film and #1 song "Tammy" made 39x more Tammys by 1958. Sequels in 1961 and 1963 kept it rolling into the top 10.
image_credit: Debbie Reynolds, 1952 photo by Bob Beerman, public domain

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: The Beatles sing "Michelle"
text: Rubber Soul (Dec 1965) brought the Beatles' French-flavored ballad "Michelle." In 1966 the name jumped from #18 to #4: about 11,000 more girls.
image_credit: The Beatles, Feb 1964, UPI photo, public domain

label: THEORY
headline: Love Story's Jenny
text: Jennifer was already #3 in 1969. Then Love Story, a bestselling novel and the year's top film, made Jenny a heroine. Jennifer held #1 for 15 years.
image_credit: Ali MacGraw, 1972 publicity photo, public domain

label: THEORY
headline: Mary drops out of the top 12
text: For the first time on record, Mary falls out of the top 12. Sociologists blame a shift from tradition to individuality, not just less religion.
image_credit: Sassoferrato, The Virgin in Prayer (1640s), public domain

label: THEORY
headline: Jessica and Amanda: soft & new-old
text: Jessica (coined by Shakespeare) rose as a "different but not too different" Jennifer. Amanda jumped 69% in 1975, maybe helped by the ballad "Amanda."
image_credit: Waylon Jennings, RCA Records photo (1973), public domain

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: Y&R's Ashley Abbott
text: Ashley, once a boy's name (Gone with the Wind's Ashley Wilkes), leapt from #17 to #4 in 1983 after soap heiress Ashley Abbott arrived in 1982.
image_credit: Eileen Davidson, photo by Mingle MediaTV (2014), CC BY-SA 2.0

label: THEORY
headline: Brittany & Samantha boom
text: Brittany had no clear trigger; it rode the '80s love of soft -y names. Samantha got a lift from Who's the Boss? tomboy Samantha Micelli (1984).
image_credit: Alyssa Milano, photo by Tom Sorensen (2011), CC BY-SA 2.0

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: Soap operas name a generation
text: Ashley, boosted by Y&R's Ashley Abbott, is now #1. Kayla, nearly unknown before Days of Our Lives' Kayla Brady (1982), joins the top 12.
image_credit: Catherine Mary Stewart, photo by Tony Shek (2012), CC BY-SA 2.0

label: THEORY
headline: Emily: #1 with no big trigger
text: Emily climbed for 15 years as a soft classic after the Jennifer era. Alexis gets tied to Dynasty's Alexis Carrington, but boomed a decade later.
image_credit: Joan Collins, photo by Frantogian (2012), CC BY-SA 3.0

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: A mermaid named Madison
text: Splash's mermaid (1984) named herself after a Madison Avenue sign, and the joke became a top-10 name. Hannah, now #2, had no single trigger.
image_credit: Daryl Hannah, World Travel & Tourism Council, CC BY 2.0

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: Friends: Rachel has baby Emma
text: In May 2002, Rachel and Ross named their TV baby Emma. Emma, already rising, jumped from #13 to #4 that year and #2 in 2003.
image_credit: Jennifer Aniston, White House/Chuck Kennedy, public domain

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: Celebrity babies revive Ava
text: Under 300 baby Avas in 1996. Then Heather Locklear (1997) and Reese Witherspoon (1999, for Ava Gardner) chose it. Now it's top 10, with Sophia.
image_credit: Ava Gardner, The Killers (1946) publicity photo, public domain

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: Grey's Anatomy's Dr. Addison
text: Kate Walsh's Dr. Addison Montgomery joined Grey's Anatomy in 2005. Addison, a Madison sound-alike, leapt from #106 to #11 in two years.
image_credit: Kate Walsh, photo by Kristin Dos Santos (2009), CC BY-SA 2.0

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: Twilight's Bella takes #1
text: Twilight's heroine Isabella "Bella" Swan hit theaters in Nov 2008. Already top 5 since 2006, Isabella took #1 in 2009.
image_credit: Kristen Stewart, photo by Nicolas Genin (2009), CC BY-SA 2.0

label: THEORY
headline: Sophia: wisdom goes #1
text: No single trigger: Sophia means "wisdom," works in English and Spanish and fits the soft -a trend. Sofia Vergara (Modern Family) added glamour.
image_credit: Sofía Vergara, photo by Keith Hinkle (2009), CC BY 2.0

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: Harper Seven & Princess Charlotte
text: The Beckhams' 2011 baby Harper Seven helped lift Harper from #119 to the top 10. Charlotte, already top 10, got a royal stamp in May 2015.
image_credit: David & Victoria Beckham, Mike Fanshawe (2019), CC BY 3.0

label: DOCUMENTED
headline: Names are spreading out
text: 1880: #1 Mary = 7.2% of girls. 2017: #1 Emma = 1.05%. Top 12 share: 25.5% down to 8.7%. Studies link it to parents wanting names that stand out.
